summary: TNF is final, so all DET@BUF live candidates are locked. PRIME's pregame Jahmyr Gibbs OVER 87.5 rushing-yards recommendation did not clear and is now preserved as a missed recommendation because no Week 2 user ticket was recorded before kickoff. The process review keeps the late Ed Oliver/T.J. Sanders defensive-line catalyst but downgrades the result-side assessment because Detroit fell into an adverse game script and the model did not sufficiently penalize the short-week workload and Detroit's starting offensive-line absences. For Sunday, no new actionable regulated-book price was independently verified for Bucky Irving receiving yards or Quinshon Judkins rushing attempts. Bucky remains WATCH because his Week 1 passing-down role was strong but Sean Tucker is back to full practice and current public projection/market evidence is still inconsistent. Judkins remains PASS_AFTER_MOVE/WATCH with PRIME's preferred re-entry limited to O12.5 at -110 or better. No new Grok pass.

decisions.reason: The pregame price discipline was valid and Buffalo's surprise Ed Oliver inactive status was real, but the recommendation did not clear. Postgame learning: the 58% fair probability was too aggressive given Detroit's short-week workload uncertainty, two starting offensive-line absences and a game script that quickly became pass-heavier. Preserve the loss without treating it as user P/L because bet_history contains no Week 2 ticket.

Week 1 usage remains bullish for receiving opportunity, but Sean Tucker has returned to full practice and no fresh regulated-book sportsbook/line/odds pair was independently verified tonight. Do not turn projection-versus-role interest into a wager without current price truth.

No fresh sportsbook-specific re-entry at O12.5/-110 or better was verified. Cleveland remains a sizeable road underdog with offensive-line uncertainty. Do not chase the previously observed 14.5 market.
